title: Block Cipher Modes Comparison
description: A static, hover-annotated SVG infographic comparing four AES block cipher modes of operation — ECB, CBC, CTR, and GCM — highlighting why ECB leaks structure and why GCM (AEAD) is the modern default.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity

learningObjectives: Compare the data flow of ECB, CBC, CTR, and GCM block cipher modes.
Explain why ECB leaks plaintext structure and why GCM provides both confidentiality and integrity.
prerequisites: What a block cipher and a symmetric key are

instructionalStrategies: Have students hover each AES box and XOR node to trace how a block is processed.
Ask which modes can encrypt blocks in parallel and which cannot, and why.

assessmentQuestions.question: Why do identical plaintext blocks produce identical ciphertext blocks in ECB?
What does GCM add on top of CTR mode, and what attack does it defend against?
